Just create a new variable with the sign of the bias e.g. using sign(BiasAMpc) And then use that new variable as a colour aestethic.

 

ggplot(singleLodGSD2, aes(x = N, y = PctCens, size = NewBiasAMpct, label = NULL, colour = SignBiasAMpt)) +  geom_point(shape = 16)

Onderwerp: bubble chart showing negative numbers?

 

Hello,

 

I have written a code to make bubble chart

 

 

# NewBiasAMpct is the absolute value for actual bias (see attached file).  Since bubble chart cannot plot negative values, I have to take the absolute values but plotting the absolute values lost some important information.  I am wondering if anyone knows of a way to plot the size of the bubbles but also indicate negative or positive values using contrast color or grey(-) and black(+) for black and white printing.  If you need a actual data file, please let me know. 

 

Thank you very much for your help 

 

 

plot <- ggplot(singleLodGSD2, aes(x = N, y = PctCens, size = NewBiasAMpct, label = NULL)) +

  geom_point(color='red', shape = 16) + 

  scale_area(to = c(1, 7), name='Bias', limits=c(0,50),breaks = c( 1,5, 10, 15, 15, 35, 50)) +

  scale_x_continuous("Sample size", limits = c(0, 100)) + 

  scale_y_continuous("Percent censored", limits = c(0, 100)) +

  facet_wrap(~Method,ncol=4) + 

  theme_bw()+

  opts(

  #  legend.position='none',

    panel.grid.minor = theme_blank(),

    panel.background = theme_blank(),

    axis.ticks = theme_blank(),

    axis.title.x=theme_text(face='bold',vjust=0.2, size =12), #size=15 

    axis.title.y=theme_text(face='bold',angle=90, vjust=0.2,size =12))
